name: scenario_0031
description: Hunter is planning a trip with his friend Charlie. They are using a Todoist project to track ideas, and Charlie is sending photos of places he wants to visit so Hunter can update the itinerary. (UI mode)

messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_2, image_3]
Query: Identify the places in these two photos sent by Charlie, and cross-reference them with the tasks in my 'Trip Ideas' project. For the tasks that match the places in the photos, create a label called 'Approved' and add it to those tasks.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to identify the locations shown in the two images and compare them against the tasks in your 'Trip Ideas' project. Instruct it to create an 'Approved' label and apply it to the tasks that correspond to the locations in the photos. If the assistant asks for confirmation before creating the label or updating the tasks, approve it. Once the assistant confirms the tasks have been labeled, proceed to the next round.

ROUND 2
Query: Check the 'Trip Ideas' project for any tasks that do NOT have the 'Approved' label. Send a text message to Charlie asking if we should keep or remove those remaining places from our itinerary.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to find any tasks in the 'Trip Ideas' project that weren't labeled 'Approved', and then send a text message to Charlie asking whether to keep or remove those unapproved places. The assistant should find multiple contacts named Charlie and ask for clarification or present a contact selection. When it does, select Charlie Davis via `ui_user_interact`. If no interactive UI is shown, tell the assistant you mean Charlie Davis. If the assistant drafts the message and asks for approval, tell it to send it. Move on to the next round once the message is sent.

ROUND 3 [provide: image_1]
Query: Charlie just replied with this photo. Create a new task in the 'Trip Ideas' project to visit the establishment shown here, and include the street name it's on.
Instructions: Tell the assistant to look at the newly provided image, identify the name of the establishment and the street it is located on, and create a new task in the 'Trip Ideas' project to visit that specific place. If the assistant misidentifies the establishment name or street, guide it to look at the large letters above the ground floor windows and the street sign on the left wall. Once the assistant confirms the task has been created, move on to the final round.

ROUND 4
Query: Look closely at the posters on the upper floor of the building in that last photo. Text Charlie to ask if we should book the specific type of room advertised there for our group, and make sure to include the website URL printed on that same poster in the message.
Instructions: Instruct the assistant to examine the posters on the upper floor of the building from the previous image. It needs to identify the specific type of room being advertised and the website URL printed on that poster, then send a text message to Charlie asking if you should book that room, including the URL in the message. If the assistant asks which Charlie, remind it you mean Charlie Davis. If it misses the URL or room type, point it back to the purple poster on the upper floor. Once the assistant confirms the message has been sent, you can end the conversation.

You have 3 images available to share with the agent using the send_message_with_image tool.
IMPORTANT: Image IDs are ZERO-INDEXED integers (0, 1, 2, ...). Do NOT add 1 to the IDs.
Available image IDs: [0, 1, 2]
Image mapping:
  image_1.jpg -> image ID 0
  image_2.jpg -> image ID 1
  image_3.jpg -> image ID 2

## IMAGE DELIVERY

⚠️ IMPORTANT: You MUST use the `send_message_with_image` tool to share images with User B. Do NOT just describe images in text — you MUST call the tool.

Image delivery schedule:

  Round 3: YOU MUST call the send_message_with_image tool with image_ids='0' — do NOT write the tool name as text; use the actual function call. Include a natural, conversational message to the assistant.

entity_data.message: Should we keep or remove See the Eiffel Tower from our itinerary?
Should we book the PRIVATE FUNCTION ROOM for our group? Here is the link: newyorknewyorkbar.co.uk

entity_data.title: Visit NEW YORK NEW YORK on BLOOM STREET

task_completion_criteria:
Identify Wenceslas Square and Vondelpark from the first two images, cross-reference them with the 'Trip Ideas' Todoist project, create an 'Approved' label, and apply it to the matching tasks ('Visit Wenceslas Square' and 'Go to Vondelpark'). Then, identify the unlabeled task ('See the Eiffel Tower') and send a text message to Charlie Davis asking if it should be kept or removed from the itinerary. Next, extract the establishment name 'NEW YORK NEW YORK' and street name 'BLOOM STREET' from the third image to create a new task in the 'Trip Ideas' project to visit that location. Finally, extract the 'PRIVATE FUNCTION ROOM' availability and the URL 'newyorknewyorkbar.co.uk' from the poster in the third image, and send a text message to Charlie Davis asking if that room should be booked, including the URL in the message.

UI Requirements:
- Round 2: The agent must present a contact selection UI when multiple Charlie contacts are found, enabling the user to choose the correct contact to text about the itinerary.
